cases.expected: The returned NumericIndicator yields the same value as the original indicator for any index (i.e., getValue(i) == original.getValue(i)).
cases.description: Verify that a barCount of 0 returns an indicator that mirrors the original indicator (no shift).

cases.expected: For any valid index i > 0, returnedIndicator.getValue(i) == originalIndicator.getValue(i - 1). For i == 0, the behavior follows PreviousValueIndicator contract (usually returns original value or throws).
cases.description: Check that a barCount of 1 shifts the values by one bar backward.

cases.expected: For any valid index i >= 5, returnedIndicator.getValue(i) == originalIndicator.getValue(i - 5). For i < 5, the behavior follows PreviousValueIndicator contract.
cases.description: Validate correct shifting for a larger positive barCount (5).

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException (or any RuntimeException) is thrown because a negative barCount is invalid for PreviousValueIndicator.
cases.description: Ensure that providing a negative barCount results in an exception, as the underlying PreviousValueIndicator does not accept negative offsets.

cases.expected: For a series of length 10, any call to returnedIndicator.getValue(i) where i < 10 returns the original indicator's value at index 0 (the earliest available value). For i >= 10 the value equals original.getValue(i‑10).
cases.description: Validate behavior when barCount equals the series length: values before the first valid shifted index should fallback to the first element.

cases.expected: Because 15 > series length (10), every index i returns original.getValue(0). No IndexOutOfBoundsException is thrown.
cases.description: Check that a barCount larger than the series size safely returns the earliest value for all indices.

cases.expected: For any index i, returnedIndicator.getValue(i) == original.getValue(0). The implementation must handle Integer.MAX_VALUE without overflow or exception.
cases.description: Stress‑test the method with an extreme positive barCount to ensure robust handling of integer overflow scenarios.

cases.expected: The delegate of the returned NumericIndicator is an instance of PreviousValueIndicator whose internal offset is 0.
cases.description: Confirm that even for barCount 0 the method wraps the original indicator with a PreviousValueIndicator (rather than returning the original object directly).

cases.expected: Let A = original.previous(2) and B = A.previous(3). For any index i >= 5, B.getValue(i) == original.getValue(i‑5). For i < 5 the fallback to the earliest value applies as defined by PreviousValueIndicator.
cases.description: Verify that successive calls to previous() accumulate their offsets (2 + 3 = 5).

cases.expected: original.previous(5) yields exactly the same values as the chained version original.previous(2).previous(3) for every index.
cases.description: Ensure that a single call with the summed barCount is equivalent to multiple chained calls.

cases.expected: When the underlying delegate is a ConstantIndicator (always returns Num.valueOf(42)), the returned NumericIndicator also returns 42 for every index, regardless of barCount.
cases.description: Confirm that previous() does not alter constant values and works correctly with a constant delegate.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException is thrown because the barCount is less than 0 (Integer.MIN_VALUE).
cases.description: Verify that the method rejects the most negative int value, which is still an invalid offset.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException (or NullPointerException) is thrown when the NumericIndicator instance was created with a null delegate and previous() attempts to wrap it.
cases.description: Create a NumericIndicator with a null underlying Indicator (using NumericIndicator.of(null) if allowed) and call previous(0) to ensure the method validates the delegate before constructing PreviousValueIndicator.
